stem.text: Consider the differential equation \( \frac{dy}{dt} = - t^{2} + y - 5 \). Without drawing it, describe the field of slope segments for this equation: where the segments are horizontal, where they have positive slope, and where they have negative slope.

answer_key.label: The segments are horizontal exactly along the parabola \( y = t^{2} + 5 \), have positive slope where \( y > t^{2} + 5 \), and have negative slope where \( y < t^{2} + 5 \).

worked_solution.text: A segment is horizontal where the right side is 0: \( - t^{2} + y - 5 = 0 \) exactly when \( y = t^{2} + 5 \), which is the parabola \( y = t^{2} + 5 \).
The right side equals \( \left(- t^{2} + y - 5\right) \), so its sign is positive where \( y > t^{2} + 5 \) and negative where \( y < t^{2} + 5 \).
worked_solution.rule_named: sign of the slope on each side of the locus

options.label: The segments are horizontal exactly along the parabola \( y = t^{2} + 5 \), have positive slope where \( y < t^{2} + 5 \), and have negative slope where \( y > t^{2} + 5 \).
options.derivation: the horizontal row located but the tilt on each side taken from the look of a familiar field instead of from a computed slope

options.label: The segments are horizontal exactly along the parabola \( y = t^{2} + 5 \), have positive slope where \( y > t^{2} + 5 \), and have negative slope where \( y < t^{2} + 5 \).
The segments are horizontal exactly along the line \( y = 5 \), have positive slope where \( y > 5 \), and have negative slope where \( y < 5 \).
options.derivation: the slope read as depending on y alone, the t term ignored, so the segments would match along horizontal lines

options.label: The segments are horizontal exactly along the parabola \( t = y^{2} + 5 \), have positive slope where \( t > y^{2} + 5 \), and have negative slope where \( t < y^{2} + 5 \).
options.derivation: each lattice point read with its coordinates exchanged, so t and y trade places
